text:
maria: @here p99 token streaming spikes and token stalls in us-west-2-gpu-pool starting ~10:12Z. lots of short-lived out-of-order packets. affecting live and dedicated pools :frowning:

infra-bot: Alert: streaming_rpc_tail_latency_p99 > 800ms for gpupool-usw2 (10m) — https://metrics.internal/redwood/streams

josh: any packet captures? looks like reorder not just loss.

maria: grabbing tcpdump from one host, saving to /tmp/rx.pcap. will upload.

angela: I see similar in canary earlier today. NIC counters show microbursts and high tx_queue drops on eth0.

samir: can you paste the tcpdump snippet? curious about seq numbers.

maria: ```bash
# tcpdump -n -r /tmp/rx.pcap | head
12:12:03.123456 IP 10.0.12.8.50051 > 10.0.11.9.43210: Flags [P.], seq 1234567:1234578, ack 987654, win 32768
12:12:03.123789 IP 10.0.11.9.43210 > 10.0.12.8.50051: Flags [.], seq 1234550:1234560, ack 1234578, win 32768 (out-of-order)
12:12:03.124012 IP 10.0.12.8.50051 > 10.0.11.9.43210: Flags [P.], seq 1234578:1234590, ack 1234560, win 32768
```

josh: yep OOO packets, small reordering windows. likely on-path NIC/ToR queuing causing re-sequencing. RDMA QP logs also show IB VLA messages around same ts.

angela: hypothesis: IO coalescing (GRO/TSO) + link-level microbursts at 10Gb -> bursts get fragmented then reassembled out-of-order at host side. firmware version on that NIC still 3.x; newer fw has patch for microburst scheduling.

debra: can we test disabling GRO/TX offload on a canary node? quick toggle:

```
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_notsent_lowat=16384
```

samir: applied to two canaries in gpupool-usw2. pushing a driver/firmware update to a third.

maria: can confirm p99 in those two fell from 820ms -> 210ms within 3m. remaining hosts still high.

josh: good quick mitigation. longer term we should coordinate NIC firmware roll, and ToR queue scheduling (pause frames + priority) with infra-net.

angela: also think enabling in-kernel reorder-tolerance for streaming RPC (smarter reassembly) could help but that's a product/runtime change.

sre-oncall-bot: Scheduled maintenance: rolling kernel driver+fw update for gpupool-usw2 on 2025-06-18T02:00:00Z, duration 2h. Migrations will be automatic. :calendar:

debra: cost note — migrated capacity to eu-west-1 during mitigation increased cross-region egress by ~2.4TB/hr. FYI billing spike.

maria: action items: (1) roll fw/drivers in gpupool-usw2 (debra/samir) (2) coord with network for ToR reflow (angela/josh) (3) add GRO/TSO toggle to node-canary runbook (maria) (4) consider runtime reorder-tolerance RFC (samir)

josh: 👍 let's keep running captures for 24h and monitor p99 and tcp_retrans/ooo counters.

maria: thanks all — will post follow-up with exact host list + fw versions. :thumbsup:
